text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Introduction pp.ix-xviii; Part I ch.1 v.1-6; Part II v.46
title: Drgganita: purpose, date, authorship
formula: Revises the Parahita system (683 CE, Kali 3785) by observation; composed Saka 1353 (1431 CE); Paramesvara observed 55 years (about 1375-1430); eclipses observed from Saka 1315. Part I: 4 chapters (days and means, epoch corrections, true planets, sines/arcs). Part II: restatement with katapayadi numerals plus tables.
notes: Five independent palm-leaf manuscripts; the edition prints numerals above the Sanskrit. Our numerals were read from those printed figures, not from the Sanskrit words.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Ahargana (days since Kali) from the Saka year
formula: Y = Saka + 3179 (Kali years); Mesa-sankranti ahargana = Y*1461/4*(1+1/42077) - 2 days (Drk year 365.258681 d); add days since Caitra for a given date
notes: Verified: Saka 1924 gives 1,863,913, equal to the book's own TS worked example (14 Jan 2002 = 1,863,823) plus 90 days. Day count at mean sunrise Ujjayini, same epoch as the engine.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.1 vv.10-23; Part II vv.2-11
title: Mean longitudes: revolutions G/H per day plus a small correction
notes: Part II v.11 states the rule: multiply the Kali days by G, divide by H, quotient = revolutions, remainder = mean. Implied sidereal periods: Sun 365.2586, Moon 27.3217, Mars 687.000, Mercury 87.970, Jupiter 4332.32, Venus 224.699, Saturn 10765.77, apogee 3232.04, node 6794.52 days. These agree closely with the Aryabhatiya-derived values already in the engine (Jupiter 4332.27, Saturn 10766.06, Venus 224.698), as expected for a revision of Parahita.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.2 vv.1-6; Part II vv.12-15
title: Corrections at the Kali epoch (dhruva)
formula: Sun +20'22"; Moon +3d15'2"; Moon apogee +3 signs -4d15'34" (= +85d44'26"); Mars +3'; Mercury -3d44'; Jupiter -2d59'; Venus -4d0'; Saturn +4d8'; node +6 signs 2d36'
notes: Part I and Part II agree. Signs for Mercury, Jupiter, Venus read as subtractive following Part I (sodhya). Node: the sum is taken from the circle (Part I ch.3 v.8, 'cakrat suddhah'). Not independently confirmed for the node.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.3 vv.1-2; Part II vv.16-17
title: Manda apsides (mandocca)
formula: Sun Mithuna 18d (78); Mars Simha 7d (127); Mercury Vrscika 10d (220); Jupiter Kanya 22d (172); Venus Mithuna 20d (80); Saturn Vrscika 26d (236); Moon: its own mean apogee
notes: All agree with the Tantrasangraha values used in the engine except Saturn: 236 here, 240 in TS.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.3 v.3, Part II v.18
title: Sighra apices
formula: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn: mean Sun. Mercury, Venus: their own mean; their 'madhya' is the mean Sun

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Tables of the manda equation, 15 values at 6-degree steps (arc-minutes)
formula: Mars 68..707; Mercury 23..215; Jupiter 32..333; Venus 18..86; Saturn 43..420; Sun 13..129; Moon 31..301 (maxima at 90 deg)
notes: Maxima agree with the TS ratios: Sun 129' (TS 3/80 rad = 129'), Moon 301' (TS 7/80), Mars 707' (TS 8/39 = 710'). The edition gives names in katapayadi; the Arabic numerals printed with them were used. Table interpolation: second order (our choice; the text gives the inverse rule in Part I ch.4 vv.9-10).

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Tables of the sighra equation: two tables per planet (Makaradi, Karkyadi)
formula: Makaradi table when the anomaly lies in Makara..Mithuna (270..90 deg), Karkyadi when in Karka..Dhanus (90..270). Maxima at 90 deg equal for both: Mars 1958, Mercury 1197, Jupiter 637, Venus 2150, Saturn 337 (arc-minutes)
notes: Two readings corrected against the editor's notes and smoothness: Venus Karkyadi 5th entry printed 2445, read 2645 (differences 927,730,505,304,179,110); Saturn Makaradi 14th entry printed 337, editor's note says 332. The five-planet tables embed the distance effect, so no separate karna is needed.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.3 vv.12-13; ch.4 vv.7-8
title: True Sun and Moon
formula: true = mean - manda equation(anomaly = mean - apogee); Sun apogee 78; Moon's own apogee
notes: Part I ch.4 also gives a divisor method (hara 266'40" Sun; 114'17" ... Moon) that is an alternative to the table; recorded, not implemented.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: True Mars, Jupiter, Saturn: four steps
formula: half manda on the mean, half sighra on that, full manda on the mean using the result, full sighra on that
notes: Same order as TS 2.26 (rule TS-EXT-4STEP): both texts use the Kerala four-step method; only the equation functions differ (table here, Rsine formula in TS).

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: True Mercury and Venus: reverse order
formula: These planets move on the sighra circle, so the order is reversed: sighra first, then manda. Implemented as: x = mean Sun + sighra(own mean - mean Sun); true = x - manda(x - apogee)
notes: The verse (vv.20-21) is stated in half-steps whose referents are not fully clear. Variants tested against a modern ephemeris: 'sighra then manda' fits Mercury best (sd 2.8 deg in 1450-1550 versus 3.9 for the TS-like order); a literal half-step reading gave Venus sd 6 deg. Interpretation choice.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
reference: Part I ch.3 v.8; Part II v.10
title: Lunar node
notes: Direction taken from 'cakrat suddhah' (subtract from the circle). Not yet checked against the modern node.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Divisor (hara) method for the equations
notes: Alternative to the tables; the verse structure is not clear enough to implement.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Arc from a given equation (inverse interpolation)
formula: subtract the nearest table entries, divide the remainder by 225 (= 15 squared) in a second-order rule

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Longitude correction and equinoctial shadow
formula: Deśāntara (longitude) correction applied to the planets; equinoctial shadow (palabhā) of the meridian line with numerals 18, 18, 2 printed in the edition (meaning not decoded)
notes: Parameśvara gives his village's latitude as Sine 647 (10 deg 51') and 18 yojanas west of the Ujjain meridian (Goladipika II 4.91).

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Secular corrections to the Grahanamandana epoch
formula: Sun and Moon corrections by period (every 200 years, 1 year, 125 years...), apogee and node adjustments
notes: Verses are also found at the end of the Grahanamandana in some manuscripts (editor's note). The numerals were not transcribed.

text: Drgganita of Paramesvara (ed. K.V. Sarma, Hoshiarpur 1963; Saka 1353 = 1431 CE)
title: Observational basis and empirical consequences
formula: At the 1000-2200 CE scan, the Drk zodiac's mean Sun coincides with the tropical mean Sun in AD 522.2 (the Parahita zero point, Kali 3623). Drk equals TS around 1400 for Mars, Jupiter, Saturn; afterwards Drk drifts from the modern sky (Mars about -0.45, Jupiter +0.6, Saturn about -0.9 deg per century relative to the Sun) while TS stays flat.
notes: Consistent with the history: Nilakantha's Tantrasangraha (1500) revised Paramesvara's constants. See validation/validation_drk_2026-10.txt.
